newsitem.title: USA: CANTV says terms of contract must remain.
newsitem.headline: CANTV says terms of contract must remain.

text.p: Compaa Annima Nacional Telfonos de Venezuela (CANTV) reiterated Sunday that the terms of its 1991 concession contract with the Venezuelan government remain in force and that there will be no changes.

Alvaro Benavides, the company's executive vice president for public affairs, also said Sunday that the company will submit information on its cost structure that the government had requested. But he noted that the cost information pertains to the rebalancing of rates for the phase-out of subsidies, and has no bearing on the rate increase sought.
On Friday, the Venezuelan government said it will first negotiate with the telephone company on second quarter rate increases and seek third party arbitration only if the discussions fail.
The government said it wanted to modify the concession contract.

But Benavides said Sunday: "We have submitted all of the information required for our April tariff increases to the government on a timely basis. Our tariff increases are linked to the wholesale price index from the previous quarter, which, in this case, results in an overall tariff increase of 4.18 percent."

Benavides also said the company has periodic rate rebalancing adjustments intended to facilitate the progressive elimination of the subsidies of local calling services by revenues derived from international and domestic long-distance.
"It is important that all sides strictly abide by the 1991 concession contract," Benavides said.
